claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric response with rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability is governed by tuning lattice distortion and electron density so that a magnetostructural transition lies close to the magnetic ordering temperature.
Bringing the magnetostructural transition close to the magnetic ordering temperature minimizes the energy barrier between phases and reduces hysteresis.
The proposed balance of lattice distortion and electron density preserves phonon and electron transport needed for rapid heat exchange.
The proposed balance of lattice distortion and electron density preserves structural integrity.
The baseline Co-Fe-Ni-Mn-type alloy has a moderate first-order magnetostructural transition near room temperature, noticeable hysteresis, and suboptimal heat-exchange kinetics.
Substitution of 2–5 at.% Cr for Fe modifies electron concentration and bonding characteristics.
Cr substitution adjusts the lattice-parameter ratio and magnetostructural coupling.
A slight change in lattice-parameter ratio or related distortion metrics modulates the strength and sharpness of the magnetostructural transition.
The proposed lattice distortion change limits internal stress and phase coexistence.
Cr strengthens specific covalent interactions that lower the latent-heat barrier.
Cr-induced electronic and bonding changes shift the magnetostructural transition closer to the Curie temperature.
Moving the magnetostructural transition closer to the Curie temperature enhances magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
Reducing internal stresses associated with abrupt lattice changes facilitates faster heat exchange and improved mechanical integrity.
Relative to the undoped baseline, the Cr-doped alloy will exhibit reduced thermal hysteresis.
Relative to the undoped baseline, the Cr-doped alloy will exhibit a significant magnetocaloric effect at lower applied fields.
Cr doping will maintain or improve mechanical stability and reduce strain-induced defects relative to the baseline.
Cr doping will enhance thermal transport and heat-exchange rate relative to the baseline.
The undoped baseline has a broader hysteresis window, requires higher fields for a comparable magnetocaloric effect, and has poorer mechanical stability under cyclic thermal and magnetic loading.
The hypothesis is expected to hold at 2–5 at.% Cr, within approximately ±10 K of the transition temperature, and at applied fields up to about 1 T.
Outside the stated composition, temperature, and field ranges, other phase transformations or degradation of heat exchange and mechanical properties may dominate.
